t: A Muslim Swahili city-state on an island with a deep harbour, trading ivory and gold for Indian cloth and Chinese porcelain.
Ibn Battuta visited in 1331; by 1500 it was among the largest and richest towns on the East African coast.
It resisted the Portuguese for nearly a century until they built Fort Jesus and took control in 1593.
dyk: Ibn Battuta noted that Mombasa’s people grew no grain on the island: they lived on bananas and fish and brought their grain from the Swahili mainland.
ev: Al-Idrisi mentions Mombasa as a small town on the coast of the Zanj
Ibn Battuta visits and describes Mombasa’s wooden mosques
Mombasa’s rulers try to seize Vasco da Gama’s ships
Francisco de Almeida sacks and burns the town
Nuno da Cunha attacks and burns Mombasa again
The Portuguese capture Mir Ali Bey and the Zimba massacre the inhabitants
The Portuguese begin Fort Jesus and install the ruler of Malindi as sultan

f.founder: Unknown; traditionally the queen Mwana Mkisi and Shehe Mvita
